A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same SimA research work. All 19 pages of each version, including figures, tables, equations, and appendices, support comparison despite substantial revisions and some internal inconsistencies.

before.justification: v1 reports original membership-inference benchmarks and a controlled study of VAE regularization, attack effectiveness, and generation fidelity (Tables 1–6 and Figure 3).

after.justification: v2 reports original SimA and SimA-MC experiments on diffusion models, including new Monte Carlo query-budget comparisons and LDM results (Tables 1–4).

M1.justification: v2 retains single-query SimA but introduces SimA-MC, which averages predicted-noise norms over Gaussian-perturbed inputs (Section 3.2, Equation 13). This adds a stochastic, multiple-query attack procedure, evaluated with 10 or 30 samples.

E1.justification: Dataset identities and the membership-inference task largely persist, but conditioning coverage narrows. v1 evaluates conditional and unconditional attacks across several settings; v2 retains paired text-conditioning results only for LAION-2B and describes the other Stable Diffusion attacks, including previously conditional-only Pokémon, as unconditional.

E2.justification: Corresponding comparisons retain PIA, PFAMI_Met, SecMI_stat, and Loss, with the same stated implementation choices and CLiD exclusion. SimA-MC is a new proposed variant. The revised mathematical description of SecMI does not establish a change to its evaluated implementation.

E3.justification: The reported ImageNet LDM comparison changes from a public pretrained checkpoint with 3k/3k ImageNet–ImageNetV2 samples to scratch training and 100k/100k ImageNet-1K samples. v2 also introduces vanilla LDM comparisons on CIFAR-10 and 64×64 CelebA, plus 10/30-query MC evaluations. These differ substantially from v1's experimental design; DDPM splits, metrics, and timestep sweep remain as stated before.

E4.justification: v2 removes the controlled β-VAE/adversarial-encoder study of privacy versus FID and the cross-experiment rank analysis (v1 Figures 3 and 5). It adds comparisons of MC sample counts. The timestep diagnostics remain, with v1 Figure 6 becoming v2 Figure 4.

E5.justification: Removing v1 Figure 5 removes its average-rank reporting with ±1σ dispersion across experiments. Both versions retain the statement that Stable Diffusion evaluations use five random member/held-out partitions. MC sample counts describe attack queries, not additional independent experimental runs or uncertainty estimates.

E6.justification: Numerous results change. Under the same stated DDPM setup, SimA AUC changes from 96.34 to 86.72 on STL10-U and from 82.85 to 91.81 on CelebA. v2 adds MC and scratch-trained LDM results, revises Stable Diffusion scores, and removes encoder/FID results. The original Guided Diffusion baseline/SimA rows and LAION-2B results remain unchanged; the differently configured LDM results are not same-setting gains.

T1.justification: The held-out-case argument replaces v1's training-point-free neighborhood with a local KDE approximation, also added explicitly in Appendix E.2. The SecMI expression loses an additive noise-residual term (v1 Equation 18; v2 Equation 19). The core Gaussian-convolution derivation and training-member limit proof remain.

C1.justification: v1's central claims about LDM robustness, encoder bottlenecks, and privacy-improving VAE regularization are removed. v2 instead emphasizes successful attacks across diffusion and latent diffusion models and claims that SimA-MC achieves state-of-the-art performance across all experiments, especially at low false-positive rates.

C2.justification: v2 removes the interpretation linking encoder regularization and adversarial training to reduced leakage with preserved generation fidelity. It adds local averaging as a stability mechanism and attributes weak MC performance on Guided Diffusion to high-dimensional sampling difficulty. Existing OOD and timestep limitations largely remain.

D1.justification: v2 newly documents hardware and software, including eight A40 GPUs and framework versions. It removes the Stable Diffusion fine-tuning budgets of 15k/50k/200k steps, the 1e-5 AdamW learning rate, augmentation details, and most of the β-VAE training recipe. The repository release statement remains unchanged.

R1.justification: Section 2 now attributes the encoder/privacy relationship to Rao et al. (2025), whereas v1 presents it as this paper's finding. References including Burgess et al., Isola et al., Karras et al., and Van Den Oord et al. disappear. Most diffusion-model, MIA, and theoretical antecedents remain.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, conclusion, and experimental narrative are substantially rewritten. v2 adds an Environment section, separates theoretical justification and method comparisons, and reorganizes the appendices. The reorganization leaves an unresolved Appendix reference and an orphaned adversarial-training paragraph under Appendix E.3.

P2.justification: Typography, author layout, and figure sizing change throughout. Main tables gain shaded MC blocks; Guided Diffusion and LDM comparisons are separated, and Stable Diffusion results are reorganized and moved into the main text. v1 Figures 3 and 5 disappear, while surviving figures are enlarged or repositioned.

improvement.justification: The MC extension, query-budget comparisons, and environment disclosure provide useful additions. However, v2 removes the controlled encoder/FID investigation and fine-tuning details for retained experiments. Its new universal MC-superiority claim also conflicts with Table 3: 30-query MC AUC is 87.33 versus single-query SimA's 89.77. These substantive gains coexist with weaker reproducibility and claim-evidence alignment, preventing a reliable judgment of net overall improvement.
